lines.text: A question that I get often is, where do I start with security in my organization?
The two places that I recommend starting are authentication and logging.
When you're doing onboarding and offboarding, you want to make sure that people that have left the company do not have access to your resources anymore.
A good way to take care of that is by rolling out SSO.
It makes sure all your applications go through a central directory so that if there is not a user in that directory, then they cannot authenticate anymore.
It also allows you to strengthen the authentication in one place.
Some of the advanced features are context awareness.
If a credential got stolen for whatever reason, and there was an authentication event done, say, on the East Coast, then all of a sudden someone tried to log in from South America.
When it's enabled and configured properly, we'll know there's no way that this person could have went from here to here in that short of a period of time.
